The differential metabolite list points most strongly to disruption of **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG map00260)** — the top RaMP-enriched pathway (FDR ≈ 0, fold enrichment ≈ 569) — with a broad secondary enrichment in **Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives (Reactome R-HSA-71291)**. The driver cluster is centred on the interconnected sulphur amino acids L-Methionine (C00073), L-Cysteine (C00097) and S-Adenosylhomocysteine (C00021), all confirmed members of the KEGG map00260 pathway. KEGG graph traversal confirmed that L-Methionine and S-Adenosylhomocysteine are linked through the canonical methylation cycle (S-Adenosylmethionine → S-Adenosylhomocysteine, two enzymatic steps), while L-Methionine reaches L-Cysteine via the cystathionine intermediate (C00073 → C02430 → C00101 → C00065 → C00097, four steps). Ornithine (C00077), also a confirmed member of map00260, is connected to L-Cysteine through a three-step KEGG path involving glutamate and 1-Pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (C00077 → C01165 → C00025 → C03912), placing it in the same metabolic neighbourhood. 2-Ketobutyric acid (C00109), confirmed in map00260, is a branching-point intermediate in threonine and methionine catabolism.

**Biological significance.** The convergence on sulphur amino-acid and one-carbon metabolism implies impaired methyl-donor availability (S-Adenosylhomocysteine accumulation blocks S-Adenosylmethionine-dependent methyltransferases) and compromised antioxidant defence, since cysteine is the rate-limiting precursor for glutathione synthesis. Ornithine elevation further suggests altered urea-cycle flux and polyamine biosynthesis, consistent with systemic shifts in nitrogen handling. (R)-Lipoic acid (C16241), also a confirmed map00260 member, participates in oxidative decarboxylation reactions linking these amino-acid pathways to mitochondrial energy metabolism. The peripheral hits — 5,6-Dihydroxyindole (melanin pathway), nitrate, and phenylephrine — likely reflect downstream consequences of oxidative stress and altered neurotransmitter metabolism rather than primary drivers. In sum, the treatment strongly perturbs the methionine–cysteine–homocysteine axis of one-carbon metabolism, with downstream effects on methylation capacity, redox homeostasis and nitrogen disposal.
